text:
The Capitals threw 47 shots at Connor Hellebuyck on Saturday, and he stopped 43 of them. That was enough on a night when New Jersey turned its own 33 shots into seven goals, won 7-4, and finished a home-and-home sweep of Washington. The Devils are 15-6 and, as The Hockey News' Mike Fink noted, four points behind Carolina for first in the Metropolitan.

The first period was a track meet. Pierre-Luc Dubois, Ryan Leonard and Anthony Beauvillier each gave Washington a lead, and each time the Devils came back, through Lenni Hameenaho and a Connor Brown power-play deflection. The Capitals led 3-2 after 20 minutes. New Jersey took over in the second: Jesper Boqvist tied it at 10:33, and Timo Meier scored on the power play at 16:18 on a shot that goes in about 8% of the time, the goal that swung the game most (win chance 53% to 74%). Nico Hischier scored shorthanded 56 seconds into the third, so fast the horn didn't go, per Fink. Ilya Protas answered on the power play 26 seconds later, but Evan Rodrigues scored on a 1% chance at 3:18 and added a late goal to finish it.

The Capitals deserved a closer night. They had 76 shot attempts to 53, the bigger share of even-strength chances (3.87 expected goals to 2.68), owned the third period, and won this game in 57% of our replays. Cole Hutson had three assists. Charlie Lindgren allowed six goals on 32 shots, about two more than those shots usually produce.

Hameenaho and Boqvist, a depth pair playing under ten minutes each, finished with three points apiece and the top two stars. Hellebuyck, in his first season in New Jersey after asking out of Winnipeg, has now beaten Washington twice in three days. For the Capitals, there's no Alex Ovechkin goal again: TSN noted this week that he had gone 11 straight without one in what he has said is his final season.
headline: Hellebuyck faces 47 shots as the Devils sweep Washington
